summary.headline: Dhoot Transmission Q2 FY27: organic revenue growth ~60% YoY, EV share 31%, FY27 growth guidance raised to 40%-45% and capex to ~Rs 750 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported strong Q2 FY27 volume growth, with wiring harness revenue up 44.6% YoY and non-wiring harness up 124%, including about Rs 160 crore from the Multilink acquisition. Organic adjusted EBITDA margin held at 15.2%, while reported margin was 14.3% after ESOP and Multilink consolidation. Pre-exceptional PAT was Rs 162 crore, up 30% YoY, and the IPO-linked debt was fully repaid with net cash, bank and FD balance at about Rs 900 crore. Capex guidance for FY27 was raised to about Rs 750 crore and revenue growth guidance to more than 40% (later stated as 40%-45%), citing customer demand well above earlier plans.

financial_highlights.value: ~60% reported growth; ~41%-42% organic after ~4%-5% copper pass-through impact
financial_highlights.change: Management cited organic growth of 41%-42% on a like-for-like basis
Y-o-Y, includes Multilink contribution of about Rs 160 crore

financial_highlights.value: Rs 589 crore of Rs 1,800 crore total sales (about 31% share); EV revenue up 108% YoY
financial_highlights.change: EV share up from 27% in Q1 and 24% in FY26
Described as consistent despite commodity cost pressure
After ~0.5% ESOP impact (Rs 9 crore in quarter) and Multilink consolidation

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash, bank and FD balance

financial_highlights.change: As reported on face of financials

segments.name: Wiring harness (ICE and EV)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 44.6% YoY; EV harness content is two harnesses (HV and LV) per vehicle versus one in ICE, with harness content per vehicle broadly similar per management. New Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar plant is running at full capacity.

segments.name: Non-wiring harness / EV components
segments.commentary: Revenue up 124% YoY including Multilink; EV non-harness revenue of about Rs 589 crore in the quarter, with a split excluding harness not disclosed on the call.

segments.name: Battery packs / assembly
segments.commentary: Two battery plants (one South, one West) added in H1 and both have commenced production; ramp-up under way for a new South India-based customer. Company assembles battery packs from customer-supplied cells and does not do BMS contracting.

segments.name: Multilink (acquired)
segments.commentary: Contributed about Rs 160 crore in Q2; current EBITDA margin cited by analyst at 10%-11%, with management saying margins will improve after integration and automation over 4-5 months, with Hosur facility to take 100% of products by April 30, 2026-27 timeline as stated.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Management expects 10%-15% annual growth over the next three years, with three new customers identified in Europe and UK; European and UK market described as flat.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised from 30% to 40%-45%, with management saying it may go beyond but is being conservative.
FY27 capex guidance raised to about Rs 750 crore from prior plan, driven by advanced capacity for IPO-funded plants and new leased plants.
EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 15%-16% for coming quarters.
Electronics and battery capex of about Rs 200 crore in FY27 (Rs 150-200 crore range discussed), part may spill into Q1 FY28.
Next three wiring harness plants to become operational around mid-2028.
EV volume growth guidance of 15%-20% for FY28 in India, with customers talking of 2x volumes over two to three years.
Receivables expected to settle at 45-55 days in the long term.
capex_capacity: Two battery manufacturing plants added in H1 FY27 (one South, one West), both commenced production.
New wiring harness plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar operational and running at full capacity.
Five new plants to be commissioned over the next 12 months, including two IPO-funded plants (advanced), two leased plants (Pune and Chennai), and one rented plant in Jhajjar.
Three additional wiring harness plants planned, expected operational around mid-2028.
Plant utilisation at about 75% on a peak-equivalent basis (two-wheeler seasonality: ~8 months at 75%, ~4 months at 100% around Diwali); last two months ran at 100%.
Multilink new Hosur facility: first products from February 1, 2027 with full transfer by April 30, 2027, with automation and new products.
demand_pricing: Two-wheeler industry grew about 16% YoY in Q2; domestic EV grew over 100% and ICE over 10%; two-wheeler exports grew about 28% (CMI data cited).
Copper and other commodity price increases passed through to customers quarter to quarter; copper inflation contributed about 4%-5% to top line.
Management expects commodity cycle to soften from the current quarter, which should help margins.
Customers guiding to significantly higher next-year volumes, with EV customers talking of 2x volumes over two to three years.
RideVision ADAS collaboration progressing; components currently imported mainly from Europe for two-, three-wheeler and CV applications.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex upsizing for, and is it EV, ICE or Multilink?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is needed across wiring harness (ICE and EV), battery, electronics and Multilink, as the company is already at full capacity; EV growth of 100% versus earlier 20%-25% expectation drove the upsizing.

qa_highlights.question: Capex breakup for battery and electronics?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined electronics and battery capex about Rs 200 crore for FY27 (Rs 150-200 crore range), segment split not disclosed; part could spill into Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Copper pass-through and organic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Copper inflation contributed about 4%-5% of top line; organic growth about 41%-42% after adjusting for this. Pass-through is quarterly and continuing.

qa_highlights.question: ESOP cost trajectory and EV non-harness revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOP cost was Rs 9 crore in Q2, normalising to about Rs 3-4 crore per quarter. EV component revenue was Rs 589 crore; ex-harness split was not given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Exit run-rate in festival months inflated receivables; management expects 45-55 days long term, normalising as monthly sales stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: BMS and battery business model?
qa_highlights.answer: Company does not do BMS contracting; it assembles battery packs from customer-supplied cells for customers 1 and 2, with no cell investment and assembly partly in-house and partly bought-in.

qa_highlights.question: Exports and EV outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports expected to grow 10%-15% annually for three years with three new European/UK customers; FY28 India EV growth conservatively 15%-20%.

risks_watch: Commodity (copper) volatility and timing of price pass-through; management expects softening from Q3.
Multilink margin gap (10%-11% versus group 15%-16%) and integration/automation timeline through April 2027.
Working capital: receivables elevated on festival-month exit run-rate; watch normalisation to 45-55 days.
Other expenses rise driven by outsourced conversion costs (contractor and piece-rate wages) as incremental volume moves to outsourcing.
Execution risk on five new plants in 12 months and three more by mid-2028; capex raised to about Rs 750 crore.
Dependence on two-wheeler and EV customer volumes; concentration with top customers.
Undisclosed details on RideVision and Hero MotoCorp (Multilink product) opportunities, which remain at premature stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes and guidance, with management raising FY27 growth and capex guidance. Evasive on several specifics: declined to split capex by segment, EV non-harness revenue ex-harness, Multilink EBITDA target, and new customer/product details, citing premature stage.
